name: Idaho
summary: The state seal on a blue field, with a red band reading 'State of Idaho' below and gold fringe. Idaho's seal is the only US state seal designed by a woman, Emma Edwards Green.
origin: Emma Edwards Green won a competition in 1891 to design the state seal. The flag with the seal was adopted in 1907; the seal was redrawn in 1957.

symbols.name: Woman and miner
symbols.description: A woman holding scales and a spear, and a miner with a pick and shovel.
symbols.meaning: Equality and justice (Idaho granted women the vote in 1896), and mining.

symbols.name: Elk head
symbols.description: An elk's head above the shield.

facts: Emma Edwards Green is the only woman to have designed a US state seal.
The seal includes a pine tree, wheat and cornucopias for Idaho's agriculture and forests.
It is often cited among the most complex state flags.
clues: A detailed seal with a woman and a miner on blue, above a red scroll.
Its seal is the only US state seal designed by a woman.
Its motto means 'Let it be perpetual'.
